company_name: Hangzhou SF Intra-city Industrial Co., Ltd.

equity_bridge.item: Investment in Xiamen Xiaoyu venture fund (47.03%, equity-accounted) at carrying value
equity_bridge.note: H1 FY2026 interim Note 17, 30 June 2026. Carrying value jumped from 53.7 to 288.6 on the HKEX IPO of one portfolio company; the mark is subject to lock-up and fund-level realisation, so it is taken at book, not grossed up, and its income is excluded from the flows (matching-asset rule).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: H1 FY2026 revenue run-rate (+14.7% YoY, intra-city order volume +30% with price/mix dilution from lower-tier cities), decelerating from the subsidy-war-boosted FY2025 (+45.4%). The 3-year revenue CAGR (30.7%) is the upper reference; the equity CAGR is not usable as a growth proxy here.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 2.9% vs revenue 3yr CAGR 30.7%: the divergence is because the company only crossed break-even in FY2023 (accumulated losses RMB2.1bn) and returned cash via buybacks and trustee purchases, so book value is not a compounding base. EPS and FCF CAGRs are undefined over 3 and 5 years because FY2020-FY2022 were loss-making; on the two years FY2023->FY2025 owner FCF grew 7.9%/yr against reported FCF 28.8%/yr.
historical_growth.notes: SBC is growing far faster than cash flow: reported FCF rose 66% over FY2023-FY2025 while owner FCF (after SBC and finance income) rose 16%; SBC went from RMB6.8m to RMB136.9m (0.05% -> 0.60% of revenue) and ran at 0.87% of revenue in H1 FY2026. Owner-FCF series (millions CNY): FY2020 -794.9, FY2021 -871.7, FY2022 -568.3, FY2023 149.1, FY2024 181.4, FY2025 173.6.

scenario_narratives.base: Revenue grows 13% in FY2026 (H1 was +14.7% against a subsidy-war-inflated H2 FY2025 base) and decelerates one point a year to 4% by year 10. The adjusted EBITDA margin (pre-SBC, excluding wealth-management and venture-fund gains) rises from 1.9% in FY2025 to 2.9% in FY2026 -- the H1 FY2026 run-rate of 2.7% plus normal H2 seasonality -- and matures at 4.2% as administrative cost dilutes with scale; the gross margin stays near 7%. SBC glides from 0.85% to 0.50% of revenue, D&A 0.30%, capex 0.35% including right-of-use renewal, working capital neutral. Cash tax starts at 30% in FY2026 (one-off payable), is sheltered at 10-20% through FY2029 by RMB780m of tax losses, then pays the 25% PRC rate. WACC 10%, terminal growth 3%, terminal value capped at 15x owner FCF.
scenario_narratives.bull: The 2025-26 subsidy war leaves platforms and chain merchants structurally more willing to outsource to a neutral third party; county-level coverage, SF Group e-commerce last-mile and parcel-return volume compound; revenue grows 20% decelerating to 5%. AI dispatch and a scaled unmanned-vehicle fleet (1,000+ vehicles today; capex 0.40% of revenue in years 2-5) take mature EBITDA to 5.5%, still below the margin of a vertically integrated platform. Loss shelter is used faster (8-18% cash tax in years 2-4). Terminal growth 3.5%, same 10% WACC and 15x cap.
scenario_narratives.bear: Meituan, Alibaba/Ele.me and JD/Dada internalise the volume they outsourced during peak surges or reopen a price war, and tighter rider social-insurance and injury-protection rules push cost of revenue up on a 6-7% gross margin. Growth falls to 8% in FY2026 and to 2.5% long-run; EBITDA slips to 2.5% and recovers only to 2.8%; SBC keeps growing to 0.9% of revenue before easing; key-account receivables stretch (WC capture -1%). Terminal growth 2%. The business stays cash-generative but earns little more than its cost of capital.

valuation_philosophy.summary: SF Intra-city is valued as a stream of owner free cash flow from a thin-margin but asset-light, debt-free delivery marketplace. The valuation deliberately strips the three things that flatter reported profit -- the RMB222m venture-fund IPO mark in H1 FY2026, fair-value gains on RMB1.1bn of wealth-management products, and RMB137m (and rising) of share-based compensation -- and puts the cash pile and the fund interest in the bridge at book instead. What is left is a business compounding revenue at low-teens rates with an EBITDA margin that has to roughly double for the base case to hold; the finding is how much of the current price is the RMB2.7bn of net cash and investments (about HKD 3.5 per share) versus the operating business.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin path: every 0.5pp of mature EBITDA margin on a 2-4% base moves the operating value by roughly a quarter; the base case assumes admin cost dilutes from 3.8% to ~2.5% of revenue.
Vertically integrated competitors (Meituan, Alibaba/Ele.me, JD/Dada) internalising outsourced volume or reigniting subsidies.
Gig-worker social-insurance and rider-welfare regulation raising cost of revenue structurally.
SBC trajectory: 0 in FY2022 to 0.87% of revenue in H1 FY2026; the model assumes it peaks here and glides down, which management has not committed to.

Tax normalisation: the model assumes the RMB780m loss shelter is largely consumed by FY2029 and the one-off H1 FY2026 current tax charge (RMB352m) does not recur; an opaque restructuring could repeat it.
Key-account and SF Group related-party concentration (Credit Customer revenue RMB452m FY2025) and receivables of ~RMB2.3bn.
The venture-fund mark (RMB289m) is an IPO-price valuation subject to lock-up; it is taken at book, not haircut.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (HKEX regular close); 52-week range 6.92-16.27. FX from Yahoo CNYHKD=X, same date.
data_sources.financials: research/9699.HK/Reports/9699.HK_Metrics.csv (FY2020-FY2025 annual, H1 FY2023-H1 FY2026; millions CNY); 9699.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt (cash-flow statement, Note 7 other gains, Note 12 tax reconciliation and unrecognised losses, diluted EPS note); 9699.HK_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt (income statement, balance sheet at 30 June 2026, Note 12 tax, Note 17 joint venture, Note 27 leases, share capital section).
data_sources.qualitative: research/9699.HK/Reports/9699.HK_Analysis.json (business model, competitive position, guidance, bull/bear cases); FY2025 chairman's letter and H1 FY2026 MD&A as summarised there.

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted-average count from the H1 FY2026 interim diluted-EPS note (920.4m; FY2025 annual diluted 920,549,124). Issued capital is 917,375,507 shares (745,610,609 H incl. 3,120,800 treasury + 171,764,898 unlisted domestic); basic weighted average is 901.9m because the employee-incentive trustee's holdings are excluded. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; the share award scheme is funded by trustee market purchases, not new issuance.
inputs.cash_note: 30 June 2026: cash and equivalents 1,279.895 + financial assets at FVPL (current; bank wealth-management products and structured deposits) 1,124.096 + short-term investment at amortised cost 50.000 = 2,453.991. Restricted cash 6.991 excluded. total_debt is lease liabilities only (13.218 non-current + 13.429 current); the company has no borrowings.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2025 finance income (interest received, inside operating cash flow). Fair-value gains on the FVPL wealth-management pile (44.381 in FY2025) are NOT deducted here because they are non-cash and already adjusted out of OCF; they are instead excluded from the forward EBITDA margin anchor (see notes).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report cash-flow reconciliation 'Equity-settled share-based payments (Note 9)' RMB136,940k (filing in RMB thousands). H1 FY2026 interim: RMB101,771k, 0.87% of revenue. No cash taxes on net-share settlement are disclosed (awards are existing H shares bought by the trustee).
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 open-market repurchases were nil; the 73.218 is the trustee's purchases of existing H shares for the share award scheme (financing outflow), i.e. the flat count IS being funded in cash. H1 FY2026 trustee purchases 96.316. FY2023/FY2024 repurchases 39.3/144.3 were cancelled or held as treasury (3.12m treasury shares remain).
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in RMB (CNY); HKEX quote in HKD. CNY->HKD 1.1749 from Yahoo CNYHKD=X at 2026-10-23T18:56Z; all per-share values are computed in CNY and converted by multiplying by 1.1749. No dual listing exists for a parity check; magnitude check: the HKD quote converts to RMB 6.81/share, a market cap of ~RMB 6.3bn against RMB 2.45bn of cash and investments, consistent with the stockanalysis.com HK$8.3bn market cap recorded in info.json at the September price.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY: 10-year China government bond ~1.8% + beta ~1.2 x China equity risk premium ~6.5-7.0% = ~9.5-10% cost of equity; no borrowings so WACC = cost of equity. Rounded to 10.0% and held identical across scenarios -- thin-margin, competitive and regulatory risk is carried in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) Leases as debt: lease liabilities (26.647) sit in total_debt/net_debt; lease principal is NOT deducted from the flows (IFRS 16 puts it in financing, so reported FCF excludes it); ongoing right-of-use renewal (~RMB15m/yr of lease cash payments, 0.065% of revenue) is carried as a capex-like charge inside capex_pct (0.35% vs 0.30% actual FY2025 capex). EBITDA is post-IFRS-16 (lease cost excluded), consistent with (A).
inputs.nci_treatment: None: all profit is attributable to owners; no non-controlling interests.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, non-US' -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). Fresh build; no prior DCF and no memory entry. SF Intra-city is an asset-light two-sided on-demand delivery marketplace earning a per-order service fee; its value is a stream of free cash flow, so the owner-FCF engine applies. Three non-operating items are kept out of the flows and handled in the bridge: (1) the RMB2.45bn cash and wealth-management pile (its finance income is stripped from last_fcf and its fair-value gains, RMB44.4m FY2025 / RMB38.3m H1 FY2026, are excluded from the EBITDA anchor); (2) the Xiamen Xiaoyu venture fund (47.03%, equity-accounted), whose RMB222.3m H1 FY2026 'share of profit' is an IPO mark on one portfolio company -- it inflated H1 net profit to RMB349m against operating profit of RMB219m and is non-cash; the fund's RMB288.6m carrying value goes into equity_bridge instead; (3) unlisted non-current FVPL/FVOCI stakes (~RMB156m at FY2025) are conservatively left out of both flows and bridge. EBITDA margin anchor (pre-SBC, ex investment gains): FY2025 438.0/22,898.6 = 1.91%; H1 FY2026 (218.6 op profit - 38.3 FV gains + 36.2 D&A + 101.8 SBC = 318.2)/11,739.5 = 2.71% vs H1 FY2025 1.72%; H2 is seasonally stronger (FY2025 H2 2.07% vs H1 1.72%), so FY2026 base is set at 2.9%. Tax: FY2025 cash tax was 0.3% of PBT because of RMB780m of unrecognised tax losses (expiring 2026-2035); in H1 FY2026 the group booked current tax of RMB352m (RMB246m paid, RMB107m payable at 30 June) offset by a RMB253m deferred credit -- a one-off restructuring-type event. The 30 June net cash already reflects the RMB246m paid; the RMB107m payable is carried in the year-1 cash tax rate (30%), after which the rate drops to a loss-sheltered 10% and ramps to the 25% PRC statutory rate by year 5 (FY2025 reconciliation: preferential 15%/20% rates save only RMB7m, R&D super-deduction RMB18m, non-deductible SBC RMB24m -> normalised ~25%). Working capital: trade receivables (~RMB2.3bn, B2B and SF Group credit customers) roughly match trade and other payables (~RMB2.2bn); FY2023-FY2025 WC swings were +126/+76/-57 on revenue increases of 2.1/3.4/7.2bn, so base capture is 0%. Price is a regular HKEX close, not an after-hours print.

bear.narrative: Meituan/Alibaba/JD internalise volume or reignite subsidies, rider social-insurance rules raise cost of revenue, growth drops to high single digits then GDP-like, and EBITDA stalls at 2.5-2.8% while SBC keeps rising toward 0.9% of revenue; receivables from key accounts stretch (WC capture -1%).

base.cash_tax_rate_note: Year 1 (FY2026) 30% carries the RMB107m income tax payable outstanding at 30 June 2026 from the one-off H1 current tax charge, on top of a loss-sheltered normal charge; years 2-4 ramp 10/15/20% as the RMB780m of unrecognised tax losses (recognised as deferred tax assets in H1 FY2026) are consumed; 25% statutory from year 5.
base.ebitda_margin_note: Adjusted EBITDA pre-SBC and ex investment gains. Anchors: FY2025 1.91%, H1 FY2026 2.71% (H1 FY2025 1.72%). Mature 4.2% implies ~3.4% EBIT margin on a 7% gross margin, i.e. admin cost falling from 3.8% to ~2.5% of revenue with scale.
base.narrative: Order growth of 15-30% a year continues to be diluted by lower-tier-city and smaller-ticket mix, so revenue compounds at 13% decelerating to 4%; network density keeps converting into margin at roughly half the H1 FY2026 pace.

bull.narrative: Platforms and brand merchants keep outsourcing to the neutral third party after the subsidy war, lower-tier counties and SF Group last-mile volume compound, and AI dispatch plus a scaled unmanned-vehicle fleet (capex 0.40% in years 2-5) lift mature EBITDA to 5.5%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: a 6-7% gross-margin intermediary whose largest competitors are vertically integrated super-apps that can run delivery as a loss-leader, plus live gig-worker regulation, means the downside axis is structural rather than cyclical. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to hold -- durable post-war outsourcing, admin leverage to a 5.5% EBITDA margin, and unmanned vehicles becoming a cost advantage -- while SBC is rising rather than falling. Base 50%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
